title: A hardware-efficient variational ansatz with an exact diagonal metric for real- and imaginary-time evolution and Haar sampling
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms depend on the geometry of their parametrised circuits: metric-aware optimisation and time evolution require the Fubini-Study metric, which has hitherto demanded costly auxiliary measurements and ill-conditioned inversions. This work introduces a hardware-efficient $n$-qubit ansatz, which parametrises states by a binary tree and whose Fubini-Study pullback metric is diagonal in closed form. Quantum natural gradient on the tree parameters, variational imaginary- and real-time evolution, and exact unitary-invariant (Haar) sampling on a symmetry sector run with no auxiliary metric circuits or matrix inversion. When the target state is supported on a subspace of $k$ computational-basis states, the redundant tree parameters carry a gauge freedom a pruning compiler converts into circuits whose two-qubit count provably grows linearly in $k$; a variant reaches near-optimal $O(nk/\log n)$ scaling with the closed-form metric intact. On electronic-structure calculations for small molecules and half-filled Hubbard quench dynamics, the method reaches reference-level accuracy with one to three orders of magnitude fewer two-qubit gates than leading alternatives. Interchangeable constructions (a Schur-transform dressing or internal reparameterisations) make the ansatz exactly spin-adapted, with fixed total spin at every parameter and no penalty terms. The bare ansatz is an exactly controllable, well-conditioned and barren-plateau-free primitive for preparing and sampling sector states: on its own, it is classically simulable in $k$ (a boundary proved for a general class of sector-sparse ansätze); composed with a classically hard dressing, it yields molecular ground states, sector-Haar benchmarking, thermal correlators, and exact effective Hamiltonians trained from energy measurements alone, with the composed circuit carrying the potential for quantum advantage.
summary: This paper presents a novel, hardware-efficient ansatz for variational quantum algorithms whose geometric metric is provably diagonal. This breakthrough eliminates the need for costly auxiliary measurements when calculating natural gradients or performing time evolution in quantum simulations. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on molecular and Hubbard models with significantly fewer gates than existing leading methods.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is overcoming the computational overhead associated with calculating the Fubini-Study metric for variational quantum algorithms used in time evolution and optimization.
main_result: The authors introduce a hardware-efficient ansatz whose Fubini-Study pullback metric is diagonal in closed form, enabling natural gradient calculations and time evolution without costly auxiliary measurements or matrix inversions.
method: They utilize a binary tree parameterization for the quantum state, deriving an exact, diagonal expression for the metric tensor that simplifies complex geometric computations into simple weight/probability tracking.
model_or_system: The method is applied to simulating electronic structure calculations for small molecules and Hubbard quench dynamics. The ansatz is designed to be spin-adapted and applicable to general quantum many-body problems.
key_observables: Fubini-Study metric, two-qubit gate count, natural gradient signal magnitude, leakage $L(\phi)$, and energy expectation values ($E$).
important_parameters: The number of qubits ($n$), the dimension of the active subspace ($k$), and the required accuracy (reference-level).
main_assumptions: The method assumes the target state is supported on a low-dimensional subspace $k \ll 2^n$ to enable parameter pruning; it also relies on the existence of structured dressings for quantum advantage.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the end-to-end pipeline, showing how the binary tree structure classifies parameters and leads to a pruned circuit whose complexity scales favorably with the active subspace size $k$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the metric bottleneck in VQAs, proposing the diagonal ansatz structure via tree parameterization, deriving the closed-form metric for time evolution/gradient calculation, demonstrating pruning efficiency, and finally validating its use on molecular and Hubbard dynamics simulations.
why_interesting: For AMO physicists working on open quantum systems or many-body dynamics, this provides a highly efficient, geometrically sound framework to implement variational methods (like VQE) that can handle complex Hamiltonians while maintaining rigorous control over optimization landscapes and computational cost.
